exercicio.statement:
Jason and Rabin are doing a chemistry experiment for a science class. They are in a step where they must add acid into a beaker, but Jason thinks the amount of acid Rabin is adding does not match with his; Jason thinks it's a little more. Use the number line to find out whether Jason is right.
Jason is using 15/8 flasks of acid.
Rabin is using 13/7 flasks of acid.
Was Jason right?

Use 1 as the reference point, then count the required sevenths to the right.
Rabin's amount is one whole plus six of the seven equal intervals after 1.
Starting at 1, move six sevenths to the right and mark that point.

nodes.description: Use the marked positions to compare 15/8 and 13/7.

hints.message: On a number line, which fraction represents more acid: the point farther left or the point farther right?
Compare the positions of the two marked points rather than comparing only their numerators.
Both quantities lie between 1 and 2. Check which marked point is closer to 2.
Read the two marks from left to right, then place the greater-than sign between the fraction on the right and the fraction on the left.

misconceptions.description: Aluno compara apenas os numeradores e ignora os denominadores
misconceptions.feedback: You compared only the numerators. Fractions also depend on their denominators, so use the marked positions on the number lines to compare the actual amounts.

misconceptions.description: Aluno julga frações pela diferença entre os números
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the fractions as equal by looking at the differences between their numbers. Compare their positions on the number lines instead.
